one_liner: CUDA SpMM and SDDMM kernels tuned for the moderate sparsity of pruned neural networks; several times faster than cuSPARSE SpMM.
what_it_does: A C++/CUDA library of sparse kernels for deep learning: CudaSpmm (CSR sparse times row-major dense, fp32, or fp16 with fp32 accumulation via half2/short2), CudaSpmmBiasRelu (SpMM fused with bias and ReLU), CudaSddmm (sampled dense-dense product, fp32), plus sparse softmax, depthwise convolution and a CSR-to-linear-index helper. Every call takes raw device pointers and a cudaStream_t, so it is a different interface from cuSPARSE: no handles, descriptors or alpha/beta, and the caller supplies a row_indices permutation used for load balancing. TensorFlow bindings live in google-research/sgk and a third-party PyTorch binding is Torch-Sputnik.
how_it_is_fast: The SpMM kernel uses a 1-D tiling scheme where a configurable number of threads (subwarp tiling) cooperate on an output tile, and it loads the sparse values, column indices and dense rows with vector instructions (float4/float2, half8/half4). To make vector loads legal on unaligned CSR rows, memory_aligner.h rounds each row's start offset down to the vector width and masks the extra leading values. Rows are processed in the caller-supplied row_indices order so that rows of similar length are scheduled together across warps and SMs, and a small heuristic (plus a lookup table of hand-picked configs for exact MobileNetV1 layer shapes) chooses tile sizes by n; the code comment says the heuristic reaches about 96% of an oracle on its synthetic RNN data.
when_to_use: Pruned DNN layers (weights 50-95% zero, i.e. density 0.05-0.5) on NVIDIA Volta or newer, where cuSPARSE SpMM is far slower than the dense GEMM
Sparse fully connected or 1x1 conv layers in inference where the fused SpMM + bias + ReLU kernel saves a pass over the output
Sparse attention or masked products that need SDDMM in fp32 with the same CSR topology as the SpMM
fp16 SpMM with fp32 accumulation when n and every row's nonzero count are even
Research baselines: Sputnik is the standard reference kernel cited by later DNN SpMM papers
when_not_to_use: Density above about 0.2 at large sizes: in the Torch-Sputnik A100 table Sputnik (13.05 at density 0.5, 7.87 at 0.25) is slower than dense cuBLAS (7.29), so use dense GEMM there
AMD, Intel or pre-Volta NVIDIA GPUs (README requires SM70+ and CUDA 10.1+), and any CPU target
Scientific SpMV or highly irregular graph matrices: the kernels and heuristics are tuned on DNN weight matrices, not SuiteSparse or power-law graphs
fp16 SDDMM, fp64, or tensor-core sparse formats such as 2:4 structured sparsity: none are provided
Projects that need a maintained dependency: archived on 2026-04-19, last commit 2020-11-04, open build issue with no answer

integration.dependencies: CUDA toolkit 10.1+, glog; the library CMake also links cudart, cuBLAS, cuBLASLt and cuSPARSE static libs (a TODO says these should be test-only); tests and benchmarks add abseil, googletest and google/benchmark submodules
integration.platforms: NVIDIA GPUs SM70+ (Volta, Turing, Ampere and later), Linux; a Dockerfile is provided
integration.thread_safety: not documented; kernels are stateless launches on a caller-given stream, and the kernel lookup table is a function-local static
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same CSR input layout as cuSPARSE, but a different C API (raw pointers, no alpha/beta or descriptors), fp32/fp16 only, row-major dense operands, and an extra row_indices permutation the caller must build

gotchas: CMake must be given -DCUDA_ARCHS (e.g. "70;80"): create_cuda_gencode_flags is called with that list, and the open issue #15 reports a CMake error at that exact line
Half-precision SpMM uses half2 values and short2 column indices, so n and the nonzero count of every row must be divisible by 2, and column indices must fit in 16 bits

Kernel choice is keyed on n (n % 4, n % 2, n == 8/16/32, n % 64) plus a table of exact (m,k,n) shapes from MobileNetV1 widths 1.3-1.8; other shapes fall back to a simple heuristic the authors flag as not general
There is no user API to build a sparse matrix from a dense float* (issue #13) and no SDDMM-to-dense conversion (issue #12); format conversion and the row permutation are the caller's job
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Sputnik over HP-SpMM-SDDMM when the sparse operand is a pruned DNN weight matrix at moderate density and you want fp16 or the fused bias+ReLU epilogue; pick HP-SpMM-SDDMM for very sparse power-law GNN graphs on recent GPUs (it is measured against cuSPARSE 12.2 on an H800). For SpMV on scientific matrices, ISpMV or the cache-aware SpMV entry fit better.
verified_claims_summary: A third-party PyTorch binding (Torch-Sputnik) times fp32 SpMM on an A100 at M=N=K=4096: Sputnik 2.52 vs cuSPARSE 10.97 at density 0.05 (about 4.4x) up to 13.05 vs 107.38 at density 0.5 (8.2x), with no time unit, CUDA version or timing method stated; at 64^3 Sputnik is about 0.005 vs 0.09. The peer-reviewed SC'20 paper is the primary evidence (3.58x geometric mean over cuSPARSE on a V100 per a search snippet; this session's search snippet adds 27% of single-precision peak and 1.2-2.1x end-to-end speedups on sparse Transformer and MobileNet), but its PDF was not opened.
status_note: Archived 2026-04-19 with no commits since 2020-11-04, but Apache-2.0, small and self-contained enough to vendor; expect to fix the CMake setup yourself for current CUDA and CMake versions.
